root_cause.text: The function `tmigr_handle_remote_cpu()` incorrectly assumes that the local softirq path has already processed all local timers, causing it to skip calling `timer_expire_remote()` when the target CPU is the local CPU (`cpu == smp_processor_id()`), even though `jiffies` can advance after global timers are handled but before expiry times are evaluated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff removes the conditional check `if (cpu != smp_processor_id())` to call `timer_expire_remote(cpu)` unconditionally, and the commit message explains: "tmigr_handle_remote_cpu() skips timer_expire_remote() when cpu == smp_processor_id(), assuming the local softirq path already handled this CPU's timers. This assumption is wrong because jiffies can advance after the handling of the CPU's global timers in run_timer_base(BASE_GLOBAL) and before tmigr_handle_remote() evaluates the expiry times."
